clue.text: To go from Dover to Calais you'll need to change stations frequently?

definitions.text: To go from Dover to Calais

blocks.clueFragment: To go from Dover to Calais
blocks.note: first meaning: to cross the English Channel by ferry or train
second meaning: to keep flicking between television stations with the remote

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing from England to France is warned that the journey involves lots of changes between railway stations.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover and Calais face each other across the English Channel; 'stations' looks like railway stops but means TV stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping across the Channel is crossing it, while flicking restlessly between television stations is the everyday sense of the compound verb.

clue.text: Ring everybody following opening of club

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter, so only that one is kept
one piece following another means it is written straight after it

blocks.note: the first letter of club
everybody is all of them

explanation.surface: Someone telephones every member just after the club opens.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to telephone them, which is a synonym of the verb meaning to phone.

clue.text: Fabulous ship's load abandoned by crew's leader

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is wanted
what is abandoned is left behind, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: a ship's load is its cargo
the first letter of crew

explanation.surface: A legendary ship's cargo has been left behind by the man in charge of its sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C from CARGO to leave ARGO. 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable or myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the legendary vessel of Jason and the Argonauts, a ship from Greek mythology and so fabled.

clue.text: Okra and plantain cultivated in a place of natural beauty

indicators.note: cultivated ground is dug over and turned, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tropical vegetables are being grown in some lovely spot in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park is a protected area of countryside preserved because of its scenery and wildlife.

clue.text: Fish alone sitting beneath citrus tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, what sits beneath another piece is written after it

blocks.note: a lemon is a citrus tree
sole means only or alone

explanation.surface: A solitary fish rests under a lemon tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a European flatfish, so it is an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Drinks dispenser - choose one with bit of class

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its first letter

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of class

explanation.surface: A bar customer is told to pick a drinks dispenser with a touch of class.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is the British name for the measuring device fixed to an upside-down spirits bottle in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs hang bottles of spirits upside down on these gadgets, which release a fixed measure of drink.

clue.text: Girl in film is stunning

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the word breaks

blocks.note: the end of film, all of is and the start of stunning

explanation.surface: A young actress looks gorgeous in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title for an unmarried young woman and is used as a word for a girl.

clue.text: Showman, one Italian chap entertaining president

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a typical Italian man's name
the usual abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: A showbiz figure, an Italian man, plays host to a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian chap' calls for a typical Italian first name, and 'entertaining' puts the president inside it, after the opening numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and stages shows, concerts or operas, which is what a showman in the business does.

clue.text: Used to support manual worker

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it
a farm or factory hand does physical labour

explanation.surface: Someone was employed to help a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like a past-tense verb, but it is an adjective meaning not new.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have previously been owned by somebody else, which is the adjective sense of used.

clue.text: To run away with companion on one is not breaking the law

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another follows it directly

blocks.note: to leg it is slang for running off
the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a friend or companion

explanation.surface: Eloping with a partner on a single occasion is not a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg it' is British slang for running away fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate is lawful and allowed, so it is within the rules rather than criminal.

clue.text: Grand piano I installed in the City

indicators.note: what is installed in something is fitted inside it

blocks.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has had a grand piano put into their place in the financial district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC; 'Grand piano' looks like a single instrument but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic means on a heroic or impressive scale, so it is a synonym of grand in the sense of large and imposing.

clue.text: Surprisingly find niece nursing prisoner privately

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not as expected, so these letters come out in another order
to nurse something is to hold it close, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to discover their niece secretly caring for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Something told in confidence is told secretly, on the understanding it will go no further, which is an adverbial idiom.

clue.text: Worry after leaving thriving business

indicators.note: one piece coming after another is written second

blocks.note: going means departing or leaving
a concern is a worry

explanation.surface: Anxiety sets in once someone has quit a successful firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a company that is trading actively and profitably, an idiom from business and accounting.

clue.text: What a PM should have, say, on vessel

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed on another sits above it and so comes first

blocks.note: to state is to say
a craft is a boat or vessel

explanation.surface: A prime minister is asked what qualities they need while aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is the Prime Minister, Britain's head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is skill in managing government affairs, a quality every head of government ought to possess.

clue.text: Carol, after collecting logs, is sleeping

indicators.note: what collects something gathers it in, so that word goes inside

blocks.note: to carol is to sing
lumber is cut timber

explanation.surface: A carol singer, having gathered firewood, is now dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumbering is the literary word for being asleep, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Tons left in USA oil centre

indicators.note: one letter put in a word sits inside it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Huge amounts of something are left lying around America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, as in abandoned, but it is the abbreviation L; Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa in Oklahoma grew rich on petroleum and once styled itself the oil capital of the world.

clue.text: One may aid healing - the spa, too, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different version of the words, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A health spa as well as some practitioner might help you get better.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats injuries by manipulating bones and muscles, a practitioner who helps the body recover.

clue.text: Who can soothe the savage beast?

definitions.text: Who can soothe the savage beast?

blocks.clueFragment: Who can soothe the savage beast?
blocks.note: surface reading: an echo of the saying that music has charms to soothe a savage breast

blocks.clueFragment: Who can soothe the savage beast?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a professional who calms people in distress, with a play on the sinister-looking split of its letters

explanation.walkthrough: THERAPIST splits as THE RAPIST, a 'savage beast'; the clue echoes Congreve's line that music has charms to soothe a savage breast.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats mental or physical troubles, helping clients feel calmer, so soothing describes the job.

clue.text: Watch featured in US magazine article?

blocks.note: Time is a weekly American news magazine
a piece is a written article

explanation.surface: A wristwatch appears in a story in an American magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece is any instrument for telling the hour, and a wristwatch is one such device.

clue.text: Copy in safe ignored

indicators.note: the letters sit within the words that follow, straddling the gap

blocks.note: the end of safe and the start of ignored

explanation.surface: A duplicate kept in a strongbox was overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to imitate or simulate a feeling or action, so it is a looser synonym of the verb copy.

clue.text: Girl drinking last of sherry, quality drink

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: Cherry is a girl's name
a brand is a kind or quality of goods
the last letter of sherry

explanation.surface: A young woman knocks back the end of her sherry, a fine drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces do not nest as 'drinking' suggests: the girl's name comes first, then BRAND, with the final Y of sherry tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry brandy is a sweet liqueur made by steeping cherries in brandy, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Fine British party

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A good British celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: In the older sense, as in brave new world, brave means splendid or excellent, matching this adjective.

clue.text: Attempt to wound with a knife

blocks.note: first meaning: a try, as in having a go at something
second meaning: to pierce someone with a blade

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sentence about trying to injure someone; 'Attempt' is a noun on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something is trying it, and a stab is also a thrust with a pointed blade.

clue.text: Look after a number, 500

blocks.note: ten is a number
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to take care of a group of five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to care for or attend to someone, the same as minding them.

clue.text: A free flat

blocks.note: taken as written
to rid is to free from something

explanation.surface: An apartment available without rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment but means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: An arid speech or book is dry and uninteresting, the same figurative sense as flat meaning lifeless.

clue.text: Puppet - see girl holding one on the wagon

indicators.note: a word holding others keeps them inside it

blocks.note: Marie is a girl's name
taken as written
TT means teetotal, and someone on the wagon has given up drink

explanation.surface: A puppet show features a young woman who has given up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE and TT go inside MARIE: MARI(ONE TT)E. TT, teetotal, is a convention for not drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet worked from above by strings, so it is one particular kind of the general term.

clue.text: Extremely short and colourful shrunken garment

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word loses its final letter
a shrunken thing has become smaller, so this word too is trimmed at the end

blocks.note: too means excessively or extremely
gay in its old sense of bright and colourful

explanation.surface: A very short, brightly coloured item of clothing has shrunk in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are curtailed: TOO becomes TO and GAY becomes GA.
explanation.definitionFit: A toga was the loose robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Type of mattress cushion

blocks.note: first meaning: a mattress stuffed with feathers
second meaning: to pamper or protect someone from hardship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cushion' looks like a noun beside the mattress, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress filled with down is one sense, and to shield someone from difficulty, as in featherbedding an industry, is the verb sense.
